premises.text: Data demand now outstrips what servers can deliver because heat throttles compute and today's cooling is inadequate
premises.evidence_span: For the first time ever, our demand for data is bigger than what technology can handle. And it's not that technology is not there. It is, but we have a new issue. The heat

premises.text: Two-phase liquid-to-gas cooling on the CPU can go below ambient/room temperature, unlike air or water cooling on the market
premises.evidence_span: this can allow us to go below ambient. That means we can go below room temperature, and there is no cooling system in the market that can do that today

premises.text: Drop-in in-cooling server integrates the two-phase system into a standard data-center form factor without facility redesign
premises.evidence_span: It's a standard server. You can insert it in any data center today, so you don't have to change a thing

premises.text: Lower CPU temperatures accelerate workloads and cut energy (~50% less time and half the energy in client tests)
premises.evidence_span: By going lower on the CPU, we both accelerate it, so we make it go faster, and we can actually make it more energy efficient

value.text: World's fastest and most efficient servers that cool the planet one server at a time
value.evidence_span: cool down the planet one server at a time

secondary_value.text: Faster, more energy-efficient compute for latency-sensitive users
secondary_value.evidence_span: run their computing task almost 50% less time, whilst using only half of the energy

causal_links.evidence_span: the solutions today are archaic and simply just not good enough
